51	## Project structure (from `uip maestro flow init`)
52	
53	```
54	<ProjectName>/
55	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
56	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
57	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings
58	├── entry-points.json       # input/output schema declarations
59	├── operate.json            # runtime options
60	└── package-descriptor.json # packaging manifest
61	```
62	
63	## Node instance
64	
65	```json
66	{
67	  "id": "rollDice",
68	  "type": "core.action.script",
69	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
70	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
71	  "inputs": {
72	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
73	  },
74	  "outputs": {
75	    "output": {
76	      "type": "object",
77	      "description": "The return value of the script",
78	      "source": "=result.response",
79	      "var": "output"
80	    },
81	    "error": {
82	      "type": "object",
83	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
84	      "source": "=result.Error",
85	      "var": "error"
86	    }
87	  }
88	}
89	```
90	
91	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
92	
93	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
94	
95	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
96	>
97	> ```
98	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
99	> ```
100	>
101	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
102	
103	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
104	>
105	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
106	
107	### Instance-specific identity fields
108	
109	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
110	
111	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
112	|-------|---------|---------|
113	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
114	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
115	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
116	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
117	
118	Example — manual start trigger:
119	
120	```json
121	{
122	  "id": "start",
123	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
124	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
125	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
126	  "inputs": {
127	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
128	  },
129	  "outputs": {
130	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "The return value of the trigger.", "source": "=result.response", "var": "output" }
131	  }
132	}
133	```
134	
135	### Node outputs
136	
137	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
138	
139	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
140	
141	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
142	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
143	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
144	
145	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
146	
147	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
148	
149	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
150	- `description` — human-readable description
151	- `source` — runtime binding expression (e.g., `"=result.response"` for the primary output, `"=result.Error"` for errors)
152	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
153	
154	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector, agent):
155	
156	```json
157	"outputs": {
158	  "output": {
159	    "type": "object",
160	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
161	    "source": "=result.response",
162	    "var": "output"
163	  },
164	  "error": {
165	    "type": "object",
166	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
167	    "source": "=result.Error",
168	    "var": "error"
169	  }
170	}
171	```
172	
173	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port:
174	
175	```json
176	"outputs": {
177	  "output": {
178	    "type": "object",
179	    "description": "The return value of the trigger.",
180	    "source": "=result.response",
181	    "var": "output"
182	  }
183	}
184	```
185	
186	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).
187	
188	## Layout
189	
190	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
191	
192	```json
193	"layout": {
194	  "nodes": {
195	    "start": {
196	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
197	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
198	      "collapsed": false
199	    },
200	    "rollDice": {
201	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
202	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
203	      "collapsed": false
204	    },
205	    "end": {
206	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
207	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
208	      "collapsed": false
209	    }
210	  }
211	}
212	```
213	
214	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
215	
216	**What format does:**
217	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
218	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
219	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
220	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
221	
222	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).
223	
224	## Edge — both ports required
225	
226	```json
227	{
228	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
229	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
230	  "sourcePort": "output",
231	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
232	  "targetPort": "input"
233	}
234	```
235	
236	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
237	>
238	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
239	
240	## Definition entry
241	
242	Every node type appearing in `nodes` must have a matching entry in `definitions`. Get the correct definition from:
243	
244	```bash
245	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
246	```
247	
248	Copy the returned node definition object into your `definitions` array. Depending on CLI/plugin version, that object may appear at `Data.Node` or as the top-level object containing fields such as `nodeType`, `version`, and `handleConfiguration`. Do not write definitions by hand — always pull from the registry to ensure schema compliance.
249	
250	## Common node types
251	
252	| Type | Purpose | Key inputs |
253	|------|---------|------------|
254	| `core.trigger.manual` | Entry point | `entryPointId` |
255	| `core.trigger.scheduled` | Recurring schedule trigger | `entryPointId`, `timerType`, `timerPreset` |
256	| `core.action.script` | Run JavaScript | `script` |
257	| `core.action.http.v2` | HTTP request | `method`, `url`, `headers`, `body` |
258	| `core.action.transform` | Map/filter/group data | `collection`, `operations` |
259	| `core.logic.decision` | If/else branch | `expression` |
260	| `core.logic.switch` | Multi-way branch | `cases` |
261	| `core.logic.loop` | Iterate collection | `collection`, `parallel` |
262	| `core.logic.merge` | Sync parallel paths | — |
263	| `core.control.end` | Graceful end | — |
264	| `core.logic.terminate` | Abort workflow | — |
265	
266	> The BPMN type for each node (e.g., `bpmn:StartEvent`, `bpmn:ScriptTask`) lives in the `definitions` entry copied from `uip maestro flow registry get`. Instances do not carry the BPMN type.
267	
268	For full details on each node (ports, inputs, outputs, when to use), see the [Author planning architecture guide](../author/references/planning-arch.md). For implementation resolution (registry lookups, connection binding, reference field resolution), see the [Author planning implementation guide](../author/references/planning-impl.md).
269	
270	Discover all available types:
271	```bash
272	uip maestro flow registry list --output json
273	uip maestro flow registry search <keyword>
274	```
275	
276	## Standard ports by node type
277	
278	| Node type | Source ports (outgoing) | Target ports (incoming) |
279	|-----------|------------------------|------------------------|
280	| `core.trigger.manual` | `output` | — |
281	| `core.action.script` | `success`, `error` | `input` |
282	| `core.action.http.v2` | `default`, `error`, `branch-{id}` (dynamic) | `input` |
283	| `core.action.transform` | `output`, `error` | `input` |
284	| `core.logic.decision` | `true`, `false` | `input` |
285	| `core.logic.switch` | `case-{id}` (dynamic), `default` | `input` |
286	| `core.logic.loop` | `success`, `output` | `input`, `loopBack` |
287	| `core.logic.merge` | `output` | `input` |
288	| `core.control.end` | — | `input` |
289	| `core.logic.terminate` | — | `input` |
290	
291	Connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes follow the same pattern as the generic action nodes above: a primary source port plus an implicit `error` port.
292	
293	Verify exact ports for any node type:
294	```bash
295	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json
296	# Look at Data.Node.handleConfiguration[].handles[].id
297	# Also check Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling — see "Implicit error port" below
298	```
299	
300	## Implicit error port on action nodes
301	
302	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
303	
304	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
305	
306	### When the error port fires
307	
308	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
309	- Request timeouts
310	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
311	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
312	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
313	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
314	
315	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`.
316	
317	### Wiring the error port
318	
319	```bash
320	# Confirm the node supports error handling
321	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
322	
323	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
324	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
325	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
326	```
327	
328	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself:
329	
330	```json
331	{
332	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
333	  "inputs": {
334	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
335	  }
336	}
337	```
338	
339	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
340	
341	### Error port vs other branching
342	
343	| Mechanism | When to use |
344	| --- | --- |
345	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
346	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
347	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
348	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |
349	
350	## Minimal working example — dice roller
351	
352	Building a flow is a two-step process: write the nodes/edges structure, then populate `definitions` from the registry.
353	
354	### Step 1 — Write nodes and edges
355	
356	Replace `<uuid>` with any generated UUID (e.g. `crypto.randomUUID()` in Node.js, or any UUID v4 generator). The same UUID must appear in `entry-points.json` as `uniqueId`. Set top-level `version` to the value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds — never hand-pick it (see [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)).
357	
358	```json
359	{
360	  "id": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5",
361	  "version": "<version from `uip maestro flow init`>",
362	  "name": "DiceRoller",
363	  "nodes": [
364	    {
365	      "id": "start",
366	      "type": "core.trigger.manual",
367	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
368	      "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
369	      "inputs": {
370	        "entryPointId": "<uuid>"
371	      },
372	      "outputs": {
373	        "output": {
374	          "type": "object",
375	          "description": "The return value of the trigger.",
376	          "source": "=result.response",
377	          "var": "output"
378	        }
379	      }
380	    },
381	    {
382	      "id": "rollDice",
383	      "type": "core.action.script",
384	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
385	      "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
386	      "inputs": {
387	        "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
388	      },
389	      "outputs": {
390	        "output": {
391	          "type": "object",
392	          "description": "The return value of the script",
393	          "source": "=result.response",
394	          "var": "output"
395	        },
396	        "error": {
397	          "type": "object",
398	          "description": "Error information if the script fails",
399	          "source": "=result.Error",
400	          "var": "error"
401	        }
402	      }
403	    },
404	    {
405	      "id": "end",
406	      "type": "core.logic.terminate",
407	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
408	      "display": { "label": "End" },
409	      "inputs": {}
410	    }
411	  ],
412	  "edges": [
413	    {
414	      "id": "edge-start-roll",
415	      "sourceNodeId": "start",
416	      "sourcePort": "output",
417	      "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
418	      "targetPort": "input"
419	    },
420	    {
421	      "id": "edge-roll-end",
422	      "sourceNodeId": "rollDice",
423	      "sourcePort": "success",
424	      "targetNodeId": "end",
425	      "targetPort": "input"
426	    }
427	  ],
428	  "definitions": [],
429	  "bindings": [],
430	  "variables": {},
431	  "layout": {
432	    "nodes": {
433	      "start": {
434	        "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
435	        "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
436	        "collapsed": false
437	      },
438	      "rollDice": {
439	        "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
440	        "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
441	        "collapsed": false
442	      },
443	      "end": {
444	        "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
445	        "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
446	        "collapsed": false
447	      }
448	    }
449	  }
450	}
451	```
452	
453	### Step 2 — Populate definitions from the registry
454	
455	Run one command per node type used in `nodes`. Copy the returned node definition object from each response into the `definitions` array, and set each matching node instance's `typeVersion` to the copied definition's exact `version`.
456	
457	```bash
458	uip maestro flow registry get core.trigger.manual --output json
459	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
460	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.terminate --output json
461	```
462	
463	The `definitions` array must contain exactly one entry per unique `type:typeVersion` used — not one per node instance. If two nodes share the same type and version, one definition covers both.
464	
465	> **Never write definitions by hand.** The registry is the authoritative source; hand-written definitions will fail validation or cause runtime errors.
466	
467	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
468	
469	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). **Do not edit this file directly** — it is auto-generated by `uip maestro flow init` and regenerated by `uip maestro flow debug` before upload. Manual edits will be overwritten.
470	
471	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
472	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes
473	- **Flow outputs**: Add output variables to the end/terminate node
474	- Downstream nodes reference inputs via `$vars.start.output.<paramName>`
475	
476	The packaging/debug step derives `entry-points.json` from these variable declarations.
477	
478	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
479	
480	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
481	
482	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
483	
484	```json
485	"bindings": [
486	  {
487	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
488	    "name": "name",
489	    "type": "string",
490	    "resource": "process",
491	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
492	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
493	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
494	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
495	  },
496	  {
497	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
498	    "name": "folderPath",
499	    "type": "string",
500	    "resource": "process",
501	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
502	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
503	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
504	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
505	  }
506	]
507	```
508	
509	**Rules:**
510	
511	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
512	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
513	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
514	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
515	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
516	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
517	
518	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
519	
520	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).
521	
522	See each resource plugin's `impl.md` for the full JSON per node type: [rpa](../author/references/plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](../author/references/plugins/agent/impl.md), [flow](../author/references/plugins/flow/impl.md), [agentic-process](../author/references/plugins/agentic-process/impl.md), [api-workflow](../author/references/plugins/api-workflow/impl.md), [hitl](../author/references/plugins/hitl/impl.md).
523	
524	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.
525	
526	## Bindings — connector connection binding
527	
528	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. This is configured in `content/bindings_v2.json`.
529	
530	See the relevant node guide in `nodes/` for the full `bindings_v2.json` schema, connection resource field reference, JSON examples, and the connection fetching workflow.

commands.result_summary:
1	# Connections
2	
3	Connections are authenticated sessions for a specific connector. They store credentials and tokens, and can be shared across automations within a folder.
4	
5	> Full command syntax and options: [uip-commands.md — Integration Service](../uip-commands.md#integration-service-is). Domain-specific usage patterns are shown inline below.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Response Fields
10	
11	| Field | Show to user? | Description |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| **`Name`** | **Yes** | Display name — always use this as the primary identifier when presenting to the user (e.g., "Salesforce Prod", "bai.li") |
14	| **`State`** | **Yes** | `Enabled` or other status. Only Enabled connections can be used. |
15	| **`IsDefault`** | **Yes** | `Yes` or `No`. Recommend the default connection but always let the user confirm. |
16	| **`Owner`** | **Yes** | Who created the connection (email) |
17	| **`Folder`** | **Yes** | Folder name this connection belongs to (e.g., "Shared", "Personal") |
18	| `ConnectorName` | **Yes** | Human-readable connector name (e.g., "Slack", "Salesforce") |
19	| `ByoaConnection` | **Yes** | `Yes` or `No`. BYOA (Bring Your Own Account) connection — customer registered their own OAuth app with the external service. Required for some webhook triggers. |
20	| `Id` | Internal | Connection UUID — use only in `--connection-id` CLI args, never show to user |
21	| `ConnectorKey` | Internal | Connector key — use only in CLI args |
22	| `FolderKey` | Internal | Folder UUID — use only in `--folder-key` CLI args, never show to user |
23	| `ElementInstanceId` | Internal | Numeric instance ID — use only in `--element-instance-id` for `uip is webhooks config` |
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Command Syntax
28	
29	`<connector-key>` is a **positional argument**, not a flag:
30	
31	```bash
32	# Correct — always pass --all-folders for discovery (see Folder Scoping below)
33	uip is connections list "uipath-salesforce-slack" --all-folders --output json
34	
35	# WRONG — there is no --connector-key flag
36	uip is connections list --connector-key "uipath-salesforce-slack"
37	```
38	
39	**Always pass a connector key.** Running `uip is connections list` with no arg returns a noisy, paginated list across every connector in the tenant and is not a useful survey step.
40	
41	**Wrong key?** If the call errors with "connector not found" or returns empty unexpectedly, look up the correct key:
42	
43	```bash
44	uip is connectors list --filter "<vendor>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	Connector keys are prefixed by source — `uipath-<vendor>-<service>` for catalog connectors, `custom-entity-*` for tenant-built. See [connectors.md — Connector Disambiguation](connectors.md#connector-disambiguation) for the full classification ladder.
48	
49	---
50	
51	## Selecting a Connection
52	
53	### Connector-Specific Overrides
54	
55	**Before applying the auto-select rule below, check this table.** If the connector key (and node-type pattern, where listed) matches an entry, read the linked file and follow its rules. Override supersedes the auto-select rule.
56	
57	| Connector key | Applies when | Override action | Detail |
58	|---|---|---|---|
59	| `uipath-microsoft-teams` | `send-bot-*` activity node types | Ask user; warn that bot scope is required | [uipath-microsoft-teams.md → Connection Selection Override](connector-overrides/uipath-microsoft-teams.md#connection-selection-override) |
60	| `uipath-salesforce-slack` | Webhook trigger node types (allow-list — excludes `button-clicked`) | Ask user; filter `--byoa` from the start | [uipath-salesforce-slack.md → Connection Selection Override](connector-overrides/uipath-salesforce-slack.md#connection-selection-override) |
61	
62	To add a new override, see [connector-overrides/README.md](connector-overrides/README.md).
63	
64	---
65	
66	**Auto-select rule (no prompt) — when all three hold:**
67	
68	- `IsDefault: Yes`
69	- `State: Enabled`
70	- `Folder` is the user's personal workspace
71	
72	Bind silently and skip the presentation steps below.
73	
74	Detect the user's personal workspace once per session — list all folders and filter for the personal type:
75	
76	```bash
77	uip or folders list --all --output json
78	# → Data: [{ Name, Key, Path, Description, Type, ParentKey }]
79	# Filter entries where Type == "Personal"
80	```
81	
82	Match `connection.FolderKey` against the personal workspace's `Key`. If the call returns multiple personal workspaces (admin tenant) or no match, fall through to the presentation flow.
83	
84	**Otherwise — present connections to the user.** Recommend the default but let the user confirm.
85	
86	### Folder Scoping (`--all-folders`)
87	
88	**Always pass `--all-folders` when discovering connections.** Without it, the CLI returns the active folder only — producing false "no connections found" results when the connection exists in another folder you can see. After the user picks a connection, capture its `FolderKey` from the response for downstream binding; do not pass `--folder-key` during discovery.
89	
90	- `--all-folders`: spans every folder you have access to. Works with or without a `<connector-key>` positional.
91	- **Mutually exclusive with `--folder` / `--folder-key`** — passing both fails with `Result: Failure`, `Message: "Conflicting folder flags..."`, exit code 1.
92	
93	### For Native Connectors
94	
95	1. List connections for the connector across all folders:
96	
97	   ```bash
98	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
99	   ```
100	
101	2. Present all enabled connections to the user using **Name, Owner, and Folder** (never UUIDs), **recommending** the default (`IsDefault: Yes`, `State: Enabled`):
102	   - "I found these connections: 1) **Salesforce Prod** by user@example.com (default, enabled, Shared folder) ← recommended 2) **Salesforce Dev** by admin@example.com (enabled, Shared folder). Which should I use?"
103	3. If only one enabled connection exists, still confirm: "I found connection **<Name>** by <Owner> in **<Folder>** folder (default, enabled). Should I use this one?"
104	4. **Verify health — ping after every selection** (auto-select and user-confirmed alike):
105	
106	   ```bash
107	   uip is connections ping "<connection-id>" --output json
108	   ```
109	
110	   If ping fails or reports not Enabled, follow step 5.
111	
112	5. If not enabled (from list `State` or ping result) → prompt user to re-authenticate via `is connections edit <id>`, then re-ping.
113	
114	6. **No connections in step 1 — bypass the cache before concluding none exist:**
115	   1. Retry with `--refresh`:
116	      ```bash
117	      uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --refresh --output json
118	      ```
119	   2. If still empty, prompt user to create one via `uip is connections create "<connector-key>"`.
120	
121	### For BYOA Connections (Webhook Triggers)
122	
123	BYOA (Bring Your Own Account) connections use an OAuth app the customer registered with the external service (e.g., a Slack app they own). Some webhook triggers require BYOA; many do not. **The requirement is per event object, not per connector** — read it from the `triggers objects` response.
124	
125	**Decision flow:**
126	
127	1. Get any enabled connection — needed only as `--connection-id` for the next call:
128	
129	   ```bash
130	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
131	   ```
132	
133	2. Query trigger objects and read the `byoaConnection` flag for the matching event:
134	
135	   ```bash
136	   uip is triggers objects "<connector-key>" "<OPERATION>" \
137	     --connection-id "<id>" --output json
138	   ```
139	
140	3. **If `byoaConnection: true`** — the connection from step 1 is not usable. Filter to BYOA across all folders:
141	
142	   ```bash
143	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --byoa --all-folders --output json
144	   ```
145	
146	   If empty, retry with `--refresh` to bypass the CLI cache:
147	
148	   ```bash
149	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --byoa --all-folders --refresh --output json
150	   ```
151	
152	   If still empty, **stop and tell the user**: "This trigger requires a BYOA connection for `<connector-key>`. None found. Create one in the Integration Service portal or with `uip is connections create "<connector-key>"`, then re-run."
153	
154	4. **If `byoaConnection: false`** — use the connection from step 1. Verify health with `uip is connections ping "<id>" --output json`.
155	
156	> Connector-specific OAuth-app setup instructions (e.g., what permissions a Slack app needs) come from the trigger's `design.textBlocks` field in the `triggers objects` response. Surface that text to the user verbatim — do not invent service-specific guidance.
157	
158	For webhook URL retrieval after the trigger is configured, see [triggers.md — Webhook URL Retrieval](triggers.md#webhook-url-retrieval).
159	
160	### For HTTP Fallback
161	
162	1. List connections for `uipath-uipath-http`
163	2. Look for a connection whose **Name** contains the target vendor (case-insensitive substring match, e.g., "Apify" matches "Apify", "Apify - Prod", "My Apify Connection")
164	3. Present matches to the user. If multiple matches → let them choose.
165	4. If no match → present all existing HTTP connections and ask the user to choose, or offer to create a new one
166	
167	> **Note:** Name-based matching is best-effort. If connection names don't follow vendor naming conventions, present all HTTP connections to the user.
168	
169	---
170	
171	## Folder Scoping
172	
173	`uip is connections list <connector-key>` defaults to filtering by the **current** folder context — results from other folders (including the user's personal workspace) are silently excluded. Empty response on the filtered side looks like:
174	
175	```json
176	{"Message":"No connections found for connector '<connector-key>'."}
177	```
178	
179	even though a connection exists in another folder.
180	
181	**Cross-folder pattern** — pass `--folder` explicitly:
182	
183	```bash
184	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --folder "<folder-name-or-key>" --output json
185	```
186	
187	**Enumerate every folder** — iterate folders and list per folder:
188	
189	```bash
190	uip or folders list --output json
191	# → for each folder, call:
192	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --folder "<folder-name-or-key>" --output json
193	```
194	
195	> If the user reports "connection exists in my personal workspace but CLI can't see it", suspect default folder filtering — re-list with `--folder` set to that workspace before creating a new connection.
196	
197	---
198	
199	## Identifying a JDBC Connection's Target DB
200	
201	For the JDBC gateway connector (`uipath-uipath-jdbc`, "Database Hub"), `connections list` does **not** expose `jdbcUrl` or `driverClass` — config is intentionally hidden. The only signal for "what DB does this JDBC connection point to?" is the connection **`name`**.
202	
203	Match case-insensitively (weak signal — surface as "likely <DB>", never "is <DB>"):
204	
205	| DB | Substrings in `connection.name` |
206	|---|---|
207	| Snowflake | `snowflake`, `sf` |
208	| Databricks | `databricks`, `dbx` |
209	| Postgres | `postgres`, `postgresql`, `pg` |
210	| MySQL | `mysql` |
211	| SQL Server | `sqlserver`, `mssql` |
212	| Oracle | `oracle` |
213	| Redshift | `redshift` |
214	| BigQuery | `bigquery`, `bq` |
215	
216	If the user explicitly named a connection in their prompt (e.g. "use the `pat_databricks` connection"), that overrides name-matching — bind it directly.
217	
218	Used by the [connectors.md — JDBC Gateway](connectors.md#jdbc-gateway--database-sql-intent) decision matrix.
219	
220	---
221	
222	## Getting a Connection's Vendor Base URL
223	
224	`uip is connections base-url <connection-id>` returns the exact vendor base URL the connection uses for proxied calls (e.g., raw `http-request` calls, Managed HTTP Request in connector mode). Manual-mode invocations don't use it. The connection must be Enabled.
225	
226	```bash
227	uip is connections base-url "<connection-id>" --output json
228	# → { "Result": "Success", "Code": "ConnectionBaseUrl",
229	#     "Data": { "ConnectionId": "<id>", "BaseUrl": "https://..." } }
230	```
231	
232	Examples across connectors:
233	
234	| Connector | Returned `BaseUrl` |
235	|---|---|
236	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<site-id>/rest/api/2` |
237	| `uipath-microsoft-outlook365` | `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0` |
238	| `uipath-uipath-marketo` | `https://<account>.mktorest.com/rest` |
239	
240	Use this whenever you need to compose a relative `url` for `http-request` or Managed HTTP Request in connector mode. See [http-request.md](http-request.md).
241	
242	---
243	
244	## Scope-Related Errors
245	
246	A connection can be `Enabled` but lack optional OAuth scopes needed for specific activities. This typically surfaces as a **403 Forbidden** error during execute.
247	
248	**Symptoms:**
249	- Connection pings successfully (`State: Enabled`)
250	- Execute fails with 403 or a vendor-specific "insufficient permissions" error
251	- The same operation works with a different connection that has broader scopes
252	
253	**Recovery:**
254	1. Inform the user that the connection may need broader OAuth scopes for this activity
255	2. Re-authorize with broader scopes: `uip is connections edit <connection-id>`
256	3. After re-auth, ping again to verify, then retry the operation
257

27	    "url": "https://api.example.com/endpoint",
28	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
29	  }' --output json

33

35	- Does **not** generate `bindings_v2.json` or a connection resource file — manual mode needs neither

42	    "authentication": "manual",
43	    "method": "GET",
44	    "url": "https://api.example.com/me",
45	    "headers": {"Authorization": "=js:`Bearer ${$vars.apiToken}`"}
46	  }' --output json
